# #002. Two-Flavor Creamery (Adding a Constraint)

<!-- section:scenario -->
An ice cream shop makes **vanilla** (`vanilla >= 0` L) and **chocolate** (`chocolate >= 0` L) using **milk** and **sugar**.

Producing 1 liter of vanilla takes `vanillaMilk` milk and `vanillaSugar` sugar for profit `vanillaProfit`. Producing 1 liter of chocolate takes `chocoMilk` milk and `chocoSugar` sugar for profit `chocoProfit`.

In the starter code, variables, the milk constraint, and the objective are already filled in — **only the sugar constraint is missing**!
1. Run the starter right away to see the red **VIOLATION** message (`Sugar used exceeds capacity`).
2. Add the missing sugar constraint (`vanillaSugar * vanilla + chocoSugar * chocolate <= sugarCap`) and run again for **AC**.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P002Input`)**: `milkCap`, `sugarCap`, `vanillaProfit`, `chocoProfit`, `vanillaMilk`, `vanillaSugar`, `chocoMilk`, `chocoSugar`
- **Output (`P002Output`)**: `{ vanilla: number, chocolate: number, totalProfit: number }`

<!-- section:example -->
When `milkCap = 90`, `sugarCap = 80`, vanilla yields `500`/L (`3` milk, `1` sugar) and chocolate yields `300`/L (`1` milk, `2` sugar):

- **Greedy by profit/liter** only makes `30` L of vanilla (hitting the milk cap) for `15,000`.
- **LP optimal mix** makes `vanilla = 20`, `chocolate = 30`, using all `90` milk and `80` sugar for **`19,000`** profit!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Copy the pattern of the `milk` constraint right above the `TODO` comment, changing `milk` to `sugar` and using `input.vanillaSugar`, `input.chocoSugar`, and `input.sugarCap`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Notice why `chocolate = 90` was picked before you added the sugar limit: `chocolate` returns `300 / 1 = 300` profit per unit of milk (vs `500 / 3 = 166.7` for vanilla), so without the sugar constraint the solver pours all milk into chocolate — exceeding sugar (`180 > 80`).

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & p_v v + p_c c \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & m_v v + m_c c \le M_{\text{cap}} \\
& s_v v + s_c c \le S_{\text{cap}} \\
& v, c \ge 0
\end{aligned}
$$

judge.m0: Output must be an object { vanilla, chocolate, totalProfit }.
judge.m1: Production quantities cannot be negative (got vanilla={p0}, chocolate={p1}).
judge.m3: Sugar used ({p0}) exceeds capacity ({p1}). Did you add the sugar capacity constraint?
judge.m4: Reported totalProfit ({p0}) does not match computed profit ({p1}).
judge.m5: Feasible mix, but total profit ({p0}) is below optimal ({p1}).
